meeting_header: Date: 2027-09-08 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Sana Patel (Redwood CSM); Alan Ruiz (VaultGenomics CTO), Priya Menon (Head of Infra), James Okoye (Security Lead), Ravi Desai (ML Eng)
summary: Initial scoping call for a 4-week pilot to validate private networking options (VPC Peering vs PrivateLink), region lock and egress constraints. Discussed success criteria (latency p95, throughput, data residency), workload sizing and benchmark approach, and a pilot timeline with clear handoffs. Customer is sensitive to egress and wants full control of outbound paths and audit logs.
topics: network connectivity options: peering vs PrivateLink (endpoint isolation)
security requirements: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML
benchmark plan: sequences, concurrency, cold vs warm
questions: Can Redwood operate without any public egress from the model hosts?
How do KV cache warmup and batching affect p95 latency for our distribution?
What telemetry/logs will be accessible in the customer's logging account?
Is PrivateLink supported in the eu-west-1 region (customer's primary) without additional infra?
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in, we're slated for 55 minutes so we'll try to cover connectivity options then benchmarks then next steps
[00:12] Alan Ruiz: thanks Maya, short intro from my side, i'm alan cto at vaultgen, we run sensitive genomic pipelines, residency and egress are like top constraints for us
[00:25] Maya Chen: totally, can you give a bit more color on what 'egress' means for you? is it outbound to internet blocked, or do you have approved destinations?
[00:36] Priya Menon: both — we only allow outbound to a few private endpoints and control via NAT. we want to avoid any model host initiating internet connections.
[00:45] Liam O'Neill: sounds like the top requirement is no uncontrolled public egress from the inference plane. we do two patterns that meet that: VPC peering (low-latency but requires route management) and PrivateLink/endpoint mode (endpoint isolation, flows through ENIs). tradeoffs attached.
[01:02] James Okoye: are there differences in auditability between them? we need full connection logs and TLS termination in our account ideally.
[01:12] Liam O'Neill: with PrivateLink we can publish an endpoint service; traffic stays over AWS backbone and you see VPC flow logs on your side. Peering works too but you must manage route propagation and there's no 'endpoint' object to restrict at the hyperplane level.
[01:28] Maya Chen: quick note — Redwood's private deployment supports customer-managed KMS, and logging can be pushed to your logging account via cross-account role. we'll share the exact trust policy.
[01:38] Priya Menon: ok good. region question: our primary region is eu-west-1, we need the model hosts to be locked there, no fallback to us-east unless we opt in.
[01:49] Liam O'Neill: we can pin the model pool to eu-west-1 for the pilot. failover policies are configurable but by default we won't cross regions unless you allow it.
[01:58] Ravi Desai: about performance — our typical prompt is ~350 tokens with 128 token responses, but we have heavy tail spikes to 2k tokens for some reranking jobs. how do you want us to size the benchmark?
[02:13] Maya Chen: perfect, that's exactly the distribution we need. for the pilot plan we'll ask for a token distribution CSV — Ravi if you can attach that to the ticket that helps. benchmark plan will use that distribution, steady-state at X concurrency and a 20% spike window for long requests.
[02:26] Alan Ruiz: success criteria: we need p95 latency < 120ms for baseline gen (350/128) and < 300ms for long tail 2k requests; cost target TBD but roughly comparable to current self-hosted costs; and proof of egress isolation.
[02:40] Sana Patel: noted, i'll summarize those. also are you looking for throughput numbers (rps) or tokens/sec?
[02:48] Alan Ruiz: both, tokens/sec is useful for our capacity planning but rps for SLA. aim for 500 concurrent short gen requests as an initial target.
[02:58] Liam O'Neill: ok we will propose a workload: 5k requests steady-state over 30 minutes with concurrency ramp to 500, then a spike window of 10 minutes with 20% long tail requests. we'll run cold start runs and warm runs to show cache effects.
[03:15] Priya Menon: in terms of networking, we currently use centralized NAT gateways in a security VPC. if we do peering we need explicit route maps; if PrivateLink we want to ensure endpoints are not internet-facing and can't egress.
[03:30] Maya Chen: understood. one thing we've seen is with peering you have full L3 visibility but you must handle asymmetric routing when you have transit gateways. PrivateLink avoids that but requires creating endpoint interfaces and may have more ENIs to manage.
[03:46] James Okoye: any constraints around port ranges or protocols? we prefer TLS over 443 only.
[03:52] Liam O'Neill: our runtime speaks TLS 443, health checks are 443 as well. we'll avoid any ephemeral arbitrary ports.
[04:00] Alan Ruiz: curious about KV cache — are you able to persist across requests in a way that reduces costs? how does that affect residency?
[04:10] Liam O'Neill: KV cache lives in-process on the inference hosts; it reduces token compute after warmup but doesn't require external storage. for private deployment everything stays in your VPC and ephemeral caches are cleared on host replacement; no external persistence unless you opt into a customer-store pattern.
[04:26] Ravi Desai: what telemetry can we get? we need per-request trace ids and token-level timing to diagnose stalls.
[04:34] Maya Chen: we stream trace ids and token timings to our observability plane and can export to your account. we'll include a sample JSON payload in the docs.
[04:45] Priya Menon: how long to set up pilot infra? we have infra folks available next week.
[04:50] Maya Chen: typical turnaround 5-7 business days to provision the Private deployment in your account with PrivateLink, quicker for peering if peering is accepted. for the full benchmark we expect 3 weeks of active testing + 1 week for analysis, so total ~4 weeks.
[05:06] Alan Ruiz: timeline sounds ok. can we do a mini-benchmark in house with a small sample before the full pilot?
[05:12] Liam O'Neill: yes we can provide a lightweight harness you can run from your side that hits a sandbox endpoint in your account — no model data leaves your VPC. gives quick sanity checks for latency.
[05:23] James Okoye: encryption at rest question — we need customer-managed KMS keys for model artifacts and logs. supported?
[05:30] Maya Chen: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported in Private. for Redwood-hosted we'll offer key-splitting and HSM options; details in the security pack.
[05:38] Ravi Desai: can you quantify expected token cost delta between peering and PrivateLink? wondering if there's a performance/cost tradeoff.
[05:45] Liam O'Neill: network cost differences are usually small vs compute. PrivateLink has per-GB interface charges; peering might have transit costs depending on your setup. we'll include a cost model in the benchmark plan with sample numbers.
[05:59] Maya Chen: ok wrapping to next steps — we'll send the detailed benchmark plan, network diagrams for both options, and a security pack. Priya will share the VPC details and James will list log retention. we'll sync next Tuesday for infra walkthrough.
[06:14] Alan Ruiz: thanks everyone, appreciate clarity on the tradeoffs. we'll compile a short internal decision matrix after you send docs.
[06:25] Maya Chen: perfect, we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule.
[06:30] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
notes: Customer emphasised strict egress control, strong preference for PrivateLink if it avoids any risk of cross-region fallback. AE/SE recommended small sandbox run before full pilot. Attendees requested token distribution and sample traces. Action items captured above.
duration_note: Transcript includes 6+ minutes of focused discussion excerpt; full call captured in recording (55m).
benchmarks_outline: 1) Workload: use customer token distribution CSV (350 tokens typical, 128 response, 20% 2k tail). 2) Runs: cold start (10 runs), warm steady-state (30m at concurrency target), spike window (10m with 20% long requests). 3) Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, KV cache hit rate, cold vs warm delta. 4) Success: p95 < 120ms short, p95 < 300ms long tail, throughput >= target tokens/sec, zero uncontrolled public egress, audit logs in customer account.
pilot_timeline: Week 0: exchange VPC info and sign scoping doc; Week 1: infra setup (PrivateLink or peering), sandbox smoke tests; Week 2-3: benchmark runs and telemetry collection; Week 4: analysis, recommendations and decision meeting.
